# Volume 1 — CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

THIRZA did not speak to Obed regarding the matter that night; however, because Nell remained disobedient on the following morning, it became necessary to explain why she was missing from the morning meal. Thirza recounted the entire tale to Obed, making a deliberate effort to make him realize just how grave Nell’s conduct had been.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0000 }

“Agatha Sowerby is an intrusive old busybody, so she deserved to be scolded,” Obed offered as a comforting reply.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0001 }

“Obed Abernethy, my surprise at you is great. Though aware of Nell’s terrible conduct, you still defend her! Next, I expect you will claim that no punishment whatsoever should be given to her!”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0002 }

“Well now—no—not quite,” Obed answered anxiously. “I suppose she should receive a bit of punishment. However, Thirza, refrain from being overly strict with her. Keep in mind that she has never possessed anybody to instruct her properly. You—you intend to provide her with food, do you not?”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0003 }

“Have you ever known me to make people starve so they would behave?” Thirza asked with indignation. “Her meals will be given to her regularly, and I am going to take them to her room personally. However, Obed, she will remain upstairs until she is ready to offer an apology to Mrs. Sowerby, and I will not change my mind.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0004 }

The meals of breakfast, dinner, and supper proved to be extremely quiet, as Nell continued to be unyielding. Following every repast, Thirza bore a laden tray up to the east gable, returning with it afterward without any remarkable reduction in its contents. Obed watched this final trip downward with a worried expression, wondering if Nell had consumed a single morsel.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0005 }

As Thirza departed that night to fetch the cattle from the rear field, Obed, who had lingered near the barns while observing, sneaked into the dwelling like a thief and tiptoed to the upper floor. Usually, Obed moved back and forth between the kitchen and the small bedchamber adjoining the corridor where he stayed; occasionally, he made an uneasy foray into the parlor or sitting room whenever the minister arrived for tea. Yet he had not set foot on the upper level of his personal residence since the spring he assisted Thirza in wallpapering the spare bedroom, which occurred four years prior.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0006 }

Stealthily walking on his tiptoes down the hallway, he lingered for a few minutes past the entrance to the east gable prior to gathering the bravery needed to knock his fingers against it and subsequently swing the door wide enough to sneak a look inside.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0007 }

Nell occupied the yellow chair beside the window, staring sadly into the garden. Her appearance was exceedingly small and miserable, which struck a pang of guilt in Obed’s heart. Shutting the door quietly, he crept over on his toes to reach her.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0008 }

“Nell,” he murmured, in the manner of someone fearing they might be heard, “how are you faring, Nell?”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0009 }

A faint smile touched Nell’s face.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0010 }

“Fairly well. A lot is imagined by me, which assists in passing the time. Naturally, it is somewhat lonely. Even so, I might as well become accustomed to it.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0011 }

Nell flashed another smile, courageously confronting the extensive duration of lonely confinement that lay ahead of her.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0012 }

Remembering the need to deliver his message quickly before Thirza might come back too soon, Obed spoke in a low voice, “Well now, Nell, wouldn’t it be best if you just got it finished and behind you?” He added softly, “You realize it is bound to happen eventually, because Thirza possesses a terrible resolve—a terrible resolve, Nell. My advice is to perform it immediately and get it done.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0013 }

“Are you saying I should express regret to Mrs. Sowerby?”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0014 }

“Yes—apologize—that’s the exact word,” Obed said with enthusiasm. “Merely make amends in a manner of speaking. That’s the point I was trying to reach.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0015 }

“I guess I might do it as a favor to you,” Nell remarked contemplatively. “Stating that I feel regret would be accurate enough, since I do feel regret at present. Last night I was not the least bit regretful. I was utterly enraged, and that rage persisted the entire night. That I am certain of, as I awakened on three occasions and felt simply irate each time. However, by this morning that had passed. My anger had vanished—and its departure left a terrible kind of emptiness, as well. I experienced such deep shame regarding my behavior. Even so, I simply was unable to consider going to express that to Mrs. Sowerby. Doing so would be deeply embarrassing. My decision was made that I would remain confined in this place indefinitely instead of doing such a thing. Even so—I would perform any action for your sake—if it is truly your desire—”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0016 }

“Indeed I do, naturally. Without your presence, it gets dreadful lonely down below. Be a dear child and simply go make amends.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0017 }

“All right,” Nell stated with a tone of resignation. “The moment Thirza returns, I will let her know that I have changed my mind.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0018 }

“Indeed—you are correct, Nell. However, keep Thirza from knowing I mentioned a word regarding it. She could believe I was meddling, and I gave my word to refrain from doing so.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0019 }

“Unamed untamed steeds will not extract the mystery from me,” Nell pledged with gravity. “In what manner would untamed steeds pull a mystery out of someone, in any case?”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0020 }

However, Obed had departed, frightened by what he had accomplished. To prevent Thirza from guessing his actions, he hurried away to the farthest end of the horse pasture. As for Thirza, when she came back to the house, she was pleasantly startled when a mournful voice called, “Thirza” from above the banisters.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0021 }

“Well?” she asked, stepping into the hall.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0022 }

“I apologize for losing my self-control and making impolite remarks, and I am prepared to visit Mrs. Sowerby to convey that to her.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0023 }

“All right.” Showing no trace of her relief, Thirza spoke briskly. She had been pondering what on earth she ought to do should Nell refuse to yield. “When the milking is done, I’ll bring you down.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0024 }

Consequently, following the milking, there were Thirza and Nell strolling along the lane, with the first standing straight and victorious, and the second slumping and gloomy. Midway down the path, however, Nell’s gloom disappeared as though by magic. Raising her head, she walked briskly onward, keeping her eyes set upon the evening sky while carrying an aura of quiet excitement. Thirza viewed this transformation with displeasure. Here was not the humble apologizer whom it was appropriate for her to bring before the aggrieved Mrs. Sowerby.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0025 }

“Nell, what is on your mind?” she inquired abruptly.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0026 }

“I am figuring out what needs to be said to Mrs. Sowerby,” Nell replied in a dreamy manner.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0027 }

Although this ought to have been pleasing, it failed to fully satisfy. Thirza remained unable to shake the feeling that her punitive plan was somehow going awry. It was entirely improper for Nell to possess an expression so ecstatic and glowing.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0028 }

Absorbed and glowing, Nell kept going up to the exact spot where Mrs. Sowerby sat knitting beside her kitchen window. At that point, the glow disappeared. Sorrowful remorse showed on all of her features. Prior to any spoken word, Nell abruptly dropped to her knees in front of the amazed Mrs. Agatha and stretched her hands out imploringly.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0029 }

“Oh, Mrs. Sowerby, my regret is so immense,” she uttered while her voice trembled slightly. “Even exhaustively reciting every word in a dictionary would fail to convey the full extent of my remorse. Your imagination will simply have to fill in the rest. My conduct toward you was atrocious—and I have brought shame upon those beloved companions, Obed and Thirza, who permitted my residence at Grey Shutters despite my not being a boy. My wickedness and lack of gratitude are appalling, making me worthy of eternal punishment and banishment by decent society. Becoming enraged simply because you imparted the truth to me was a deeply evil act. Indeed, it was the truth; absolute veracity marked your every word. Red describes my hair, and my appearance is freckled, scrawny, and hideous. Likewise, truth backed my own statements to you, yet they ought to have remained unspoken. Oh, Mrs. Sowerby, I beg, I beg of you to bestow your forgiveness upon me. Denying it would inflict permanent grief upon a helpless young orphan girl, a fate you surely would not wish even upon one with a horrific temper, would you? Oh, my heart tells me you could not. Mrs. Sowerby, please declare that I am forgiven.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0030 }

Nell pressed her hands together, bent her head downward, and stood awaiting the verdict.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0031 }

Her truthfulness was beyond doubt, emanating from every nuance of her vocal expression. This authentic quality was perceived by both Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby. However, the first of them realized with consternation that Nell was truly taking delight in her period of disgrace—that she was delighting in the complete nature of her degradation. What had become of the beneficial chastisement for which she, Thirza, had congratulated herself? Nell had transformed it into a form of definite enjoyment.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0032 }

The kindly, if rather meddlesome, heart of good Mrs. Sowerby lacked the sharpness of perception to notice this. All she observed was the completely exhaustive nature of Nell’s apology, which caused every bit of her anger to disappear.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0033 }

“Come, come, stand up, little one,” she stated warmly. “Naturally, you have my forgiveness. It seems I was likely somewhat overly strict with you, regardless. However, I am simply quite a candid individual. You simply must not pay me any heed, that is all. No one can dispute that your hair is exceedingly red; nevertheless, I used to know a female—we actually attended school together—who possessed hair precisely as red as yours in her youth, yet it deepened into a truly lovely auburn as she matured. It would not amaze me in the slightest if the same thing happened to yours—not in the slightest.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0034 }

“Oh, Mrs. Sowerby!” Nell inhaled deeply while standing up. “You have offered me hope. I will forever consider you a benefactor. Oh, I would be able to bear anything provided I just believed my hair was going to turn a handsome auburn once I was grown up. Would it not be far simpler to be good if a person possessed a handsome auburn hair, don’t you think? And now would it be all right if I went out into your garden to sit upon the bench beneath the apple-trees while Thirza and you discuss things? There exists far greater room for imagination in that spot.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0035 }

“Mercy, indeed, run on, little one. Furthermore, you may gather a bunch of those white June lilies located in the corner if you wish.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0036 }

When the door shut after Nell, a lamp was promptly lit by Mrs. Sowerby as she rose.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0037 }

“She is truly a peculiar little child. Thirza, move to this chair, which offers more comfort than the one you are currently using; that one is merely reserved for the hired boy's use. Indeed, her behavior is undeniably strange, yet she possesses an appealing quality regardless. My astonishment at you and Obed deciding to raise her has diminished from what it once was—and my pity for both of you has lessened too. It is possible she will turn out fine. Naturally, her manner of speaking is unusual—a bit overly—well, rather too forceful, as you are aware; nevertheless, she will probably outgrow that trait now that her life is spent among civilized people. Furthermore, I suspect she possesses a rather swift temper; yet one reassuring thought is that a youngster with a fiery temper, who simply flares up and then settles down, is not at all prone to being cunning or dishonest. May I be spared from a deceitful child, above all else. When all is considered, Thirza, I am somewhat fond of her.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0038 }

As Thirza departed for her house, Nell emerged from the sweet-smelling dusk of the orchard, holding a bundle of white narcissi in her hands.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0039 }

“Did I not make a rather good apology?” she inquired with pride while they walked along the lane. “It occurred to me that as long as I was required to perform the task, I ought to accomplish it completely.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0040 }

“You certainly did a complete job of it,” commented Thirza. Finding that she was disposed to giggle at the memory filled Thirza with consternation. A troubling sense that she should reprimand Nell for offering such an effective apology also came over her; yet, such an action would be absurd! Saying sternly, she struck a middle ground with her moral sense:
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0041 }

“It is my hope that you will not need to offer numerous further excuses of this nature. My wish is that you will endeavor to govern your passion from this point on, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0042 }

“If folks didn't tease me regarding my appearance, that would be less difficult,” Nell said, sighing. “Other matters do not make me angry; yet being mocked about my hair exhausts me so much that it simply causes me to explode with rage. Is it your opinion that my hair will truly turn into a lovely auburn once I am older?”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0043 }

“Nell, your appearance shouldn't occupy your thoughts to such a degree. It worries me that you are an exceedingly vain young girl.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0044 }

“In what way am I capable of vanity if my own plainness is clear to me?” Nell objected. “Beautiful items are my passion; and staring into the mirror only to behold an unlovely image fills me with distaste. A deep sadness comes over me—the exact sensation I experience whenever I view something repulsive. My compassion goes out to it for its lack of beauty.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0045 }

“Handsome is as handsome does,” Thirza quoted. “That has been told to me previously, yet I am dubious regarding its truth,” skeptical Nell observed, smelling her narcissi. “Oh, these blossoms are so sweet! Mrs. Sowerby was very kind to present them to me. At present, I harbour no resentment toward Mrs. Sowerby. Expressing regret and receiving pardon bestows a delightful, soothing sensation, doesn’t it? Are not the stars brilliant this evening? Were it possible to dwell within a star, which would be your choice? I would prefer that beautiful, bright, large one far off in that direction, situated atop that dark hill.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0046 }

“Nell, do hold your tongue,” said Thirza, who was completely exhausted from attempting to keep up with the twists and turns of Nell’s mind.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0047 }

Nell uttered nothing else prior to their turning into the lane that belonged to them. Down it to encounter them came a slight gypsy wind, filled with the spicy fragrance of dew-moistened young ferns. High up amidst the darkness, from the kitchen situated at Grey Shutters, a bright light shone through the trees. Nell abruptly drew near Thirza and slid her own hand inside the hardened palm of the older woman.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0048 }

“Going back to a place I know is truly home feels wonderful,” she remarked. “Grey Shutters has my love already, even though I have never cared for anywhere else before. Not a single place ever felt like home to me. Oh, Thirza, my happiness is so great. I could offer up a prayer this very minute without struggling in the slightest.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0049 }

As those slender fingers met hers, a gentle, comforting feeling overflowed within Thirza, perhaps representing a pulse of the motherhood she had never known. The sheer unfamiliarity and delight of the sensation rattled her. To regain her usual tranquility, she hurried to deliver a moral lesson.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0050 }

“Provided that you act as a good girl, Nell, happiness will always be yours. Furthermore, uttering your prayers ought never to be a difficult thing for you.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0051 }

“Uttering one’s prayers does not quite equate to praying,” Nell remarked thoughtfully. “However, I am about to pretend that I am the wind that blows up above in the tops of those trees. Once I grow weary of the trees, I will pretend that I am swaying softly down here among the ferns—and next I will soar across to Mrs. Sowerby’s garden and make the flowers dance—and after that I will rush in a single huge swoop across the clover field—and then I will sweep across the Lake of Glassy Waters and stir it completely into small, glittering waves. Oh, a wind offers such immense possibilities for imagination! Therefore, I will refrain from speaking any longer at present, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0052 }

“Thanks be to goodness for that,” Thirza breathed in devout relief.
{: #nw-v01-c10-p0053 }
